insight: Specs over data modules in `desktop/src` are stub-passable whenever the expected value is read back out of the module under test (`toBe(profile.cliInstall.unix)`), so catalog contents must be asserted as literal strings.

Functions in `desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` that take `&AppHandle` to read `app.path()` cannot be exercised by any spec because `tauri` is declared with `features = []` in Cargo.toml (no `test` feature, so no `mock_app`), so a plan that asserts resolution-order behavior must require the candidate directory list be injectable — otherwise the specs silently degrade into testing an array the test itself built.

The desktop package's `pnpm test` covers only pure logic (`test/rules.test.ts`, `test/catalog.test.ts`) and vite.config has no jsdom/happy-dom environment, so any plan touching `desktop/src/main.ts` or `desktop/index.html` must add a manual verification step — a UI control can be deleted with every gate green.

The Tauri config sets `"csp": null` and main.ts builds several elements via `innerHTML`, so any new `#[tauri::command]` that accepts a free-form string and executes it (shell, path, URL) hands the webview that authority directly — prefer commands that take an identifier and resolve the dangerous value Rust-side.
